newsitem.title: SPAIN: RALLYING-LIATTI AND MAKINEN IN CATALUNYA RALLY DUEL.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-LIATTI AND MAKINEN IN CATALUNYA RALLY DUEL.

text.p: Italian Piero Liatti and reigning world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland shared the lead after the second day of the Catalunya Rally on Tuesday.
As overnight leader Colin McRae of Britain dropped out of contention with a puncture on the 11th stage, Makinen in a Mitsubishi and Liatti in a Subaru continually matched each other for pace.
Both completed the first 13 stages with a time of three hours three minutes 56 seconds with the prospect of a thrilling finale back in the mountains on Wednesday.
"I have had no problems all day and have been pushing all the way," said Liatti, who took the lead from McRae on the 10th stage.
"The only drama was when I hit a rock on the eighth stage and I wasn't sure what damage that had done, so I took it steady for about a kilometre.
The Peugeot team continued to impress the world rally championship regulars with Frenchman Gilles Panizzi claiming third place after a climb up the field from ninth overnight.
He had led for much of the opening day before a puncture on stage six cost him more than two minutes.
McRae recovered from his puncture to set the fastest time on the 13th stage and ended the leg fourth overall, more than a minute behind Panizzi.
"Tyre wear has been critical and, although we have been trying to look after them, I had to push hard because Tommi and Piero were pushing me," explained McRae.
"On stage 11 we suffered the puncture and, although we were nearing the end of the stage, it would have been silly to continue because the next stage was a long one.
"I am obviously hugely disappointed, but we will still be giving everything because anything can still happen."
Other championship contenders had a frustrating day, with both Ford drivers suffering transmission failures after brake problems had ruined their first day.

Local hero Carlo Sainz, who suffered two punctures on the day's first stage, was already beginning to drop back from the leading three drivers when he lost five minutes on the 10th stage with a broken propshaft.
He recovered with the fastest time on the 11th stage and ended the day 10th, but with little hope of recovering the time lost to leaders Liatti and Makinen.
"I am feeling a lot more confident with the car now, but all we can really do is try and pick up a few more places for championship points," said Sainz.

Sainz's German team mate Armin Schwarz had been the only championship challenger to finish the first four rounds of the season, but his luck ran out on the seventh stage when his car filled with smoke from a split silencer box.

The heat from the exhaust then broke his propshaft on the following Prades run, although he was able to reach the next service point for urgent repairs. But Schwarz retired for good on the ninth stage, when the propshaft snapped again.

"I am obviously disappointed because this was the first time I have retired this season, but there was no chance of continuing because there was another long stage after the one we hit problems on," he said.
